title: "Implementing the passage-level Student-t model in Stan"

[Stan](https://mc-stan.org/) samples a posterior after the analyst declares data, parameters, and density contributions. The passage-level Student-t program below corresponds exactly to the robust model introduced on the [nonconjugate-posterior page](beyond-conjugacy.qmd).

## The complete program

```stan
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  vector[N] y;
  real<lower=0> prior_mu_sd;
  real<lower=0> prior_sigma_sd;
  real<lower=2> nu;
}

parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
  mu ~ normal(0, prior_mu_sd);
  sigma ~ normal(0, prior_sigma_sd);
  y ~ student_t(nu, mu, sigma);
}

generated quantities {
  real geometric_duration_ratio = exp(mu);
  array[N] real y_rep;
  vector[N] log_lik;

  for (n in 1:N) {
    y_rep[n] = student_t_rng(nu, mu, sigma);
    log_lik[n] = student_t_lpdf(y[n] | nu, mu, sigma);
  }
}
```

The data block contains the 55 observed passage contrasts and the empirically calibrated prior scales. The parameters block declares the unknown location and positive scale. In the model block, each tilde statement adds a log-density contribution to Stan's `target`; it does not simulate a value.

The half-normal prior is represented by the lower bound on `sigma` together with a zero-centered normal density. Stan transforms this constrained parameter internally and applies the required Jacobian on its unconstrained sampling scale.

## Preparing the observed data

```{r}
#| label: prepare-provo-stan-data
library(posterior)

provo <- read.csv("data/provo/passage-summaries.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
y <- provo$noun_minus_verb_log_ffd
stan_data <- list(
  N = length(y),
  y = y,
  prior_mu_sd = 2 * sd(y),
  prior_sigma_sd = 2 * sd(y),
  nu = 4
)

stopifnot(stan_data$N == 55L, all(is.finite(stan_data$y)))
str(stan_data)
```

## Fitting the exact model

The reference run uses four data-scaled initial values constructed from the posterior grid covariance shown on the [mass-matrix page](mass-matrix-geometry.qmd). The code below reconstructs those values from the observed Provo contrasts rather than relying on an undeclared helper.

```{r}
#| label: construct-provo-stan-initial-values
log_posterior_eta <- function(eta) {
  mu <- eta[[1L]]
  sigma <- exp(eta[[2L]])
  sum(dt((y - mu) / sigma, df = stan_data$nu, log = TRUE) - log(sigma)) +
    dnorm(mu, 0, stan_data$prior_mu_sd, log = TRUE) +
    log(2) + dnorm(sigma, 0, stan_data$prior_sigma_sd, log = TRUE) +
    eta[[2L]]
}

gradient_log_posterior_eta <- function(eta) {
  mu <- eta[[1L]]
  sigma <- exp(eta[[2L]])
  residual <- y - mu
  scaled_squared <- residual^2 / sigma^2
  c(
    sum((stan_data$nu + 1) * residual /
          (stan_data$nu * sigma^2 + residual^2)) -
      mu / stan_data$prior_mu_sd^2,
    sum(-1 + (stan_data$nu + 1) * scaled_squared /
          (stan_data$nu + scaled_squared)) -
      sigma^2 / stan_data$prior_sigma_sd^2 + 1
  )
}

mode_fit <- optim(
  c(median(y), log(mad(y))),
  function(eta) -log_posterior_eta(eta),
  gr = function(eta) -gradient_log_posterior_eta(eta),
  method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE,
  control = list(reltol = 1e-12, maxit = 1000L)
)
mode_eta <- unname(mode_fit$par)
mode_covariance <- solve(mode_fit$hessian)
grid_sd <- sqrt(diag(mode_covariance))
posterior_grid <- expand.grid(
  mu = seq(mode_eta[[1L]] - 7 * grid_sd[[1L]],
           mode_eta[[1L]] + 7 * grid_sd[[1L]], length.out = 321L),
  log_sigma = seq(mode_eta[[2L]] - 7 * grid_sd[[2L]],
                  mode_eta[[2L]] + 7 * grid_sd[[2L]], length.out = 321L)
)
posterior_grid$log_kernel <- apply(posterior_grid, 1L, log_posterior_eta)
posterior_grid$weight <- exp(
  posterior_grid$log_kernel - max(posterior_grid$log_kernel)
)
posterior_grid$weight <- posterior_grid$weight / sum(posterior_grid$weight)
grid_mean_eta <- colSums(posterior_grid * posterior_grid$weight)
grid_centered <- sweep(as.matrix(posterior_grid[, c("mu", "log_sigma")]),
                       2L, grid_mean_eta, "-")
grid_covariance <- crossprod(grid_centered * sqrt(posterior_grid$weight))

initial_values <- function(offsets) {
  lapply(offsets, function(offset) list(
    mu = mode_eta[[1L]] + offset * sqrt(grid_covariance[1L, 1L]),
    sigma = exp(mode_eta[[2L]] +
                  offset * sqrt(grid_covariance[2L, 2L]))
  ))
}

stopifnot(mode_fit$convergence == 0L)
stan_offsets <- seq(-.75, .75, length.out = 4L)
do.call(rbind, initial_values(stan_offsets))
```

The sampling call is then fully specified by the observed data, the program, and these initial values.

```{r}
#| label: show-provo-stan-fit
#| eval: false
library(cmdstanr)

model <- cmdstan_model(
  "scripts/data-grounding/reference_inference_bayesian.stan",
  quiet = TRUE
)

fit <- model$sample(
  data = stan_data,
  seed = 2026101806,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = 4,
  iter_warmup = 750,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  adapt_delta = .90,
  max_treedepth = 10,
  init = initial_values(stan_offsets),
  refresh = 0,
  output_dir = tempdir()
)
```

The evaluated page reads the frozen draw object from that exact run. The cache key includes the Provo checksum, Stan-program checksum, CmdStan version, algorithm settings, and initialization specification, so changed inputs cannot silently reuse these draws.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-provo-stan-fit
cache <- readRDS(
  "data/provo/provo-stan-draw-cache.rds"
)
production <- subset_draws(
  cache$production_draws,
  variable = c("mu", "sigma", "geometric_duration_ratio")
)
fit_summary <- as.data.frame(summarise_draws(
  production,
  "mean", "median", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail",
  ~quantile2(.x, probs = c(.025, .975))
))
production_diagnostics <- as.data.frame(
  as_draws_df(cache$production_diagnostics)
)

stopifnot(max(fit_summary$rhat) < 1.01,
          sum(production_diagnostics$divergent__) == 0L)
fit_summary
```

The fitted mean of $\mu$ is `r sprintf("%.6f", fit_summary$mean[fit_summary$variable == "mu"])`, and the geometric-scale ratio has mean `r sprintf("%.6f", fit_summary$mean[fit_summary$variable == "geometric_duration_ratio"])`. These are passage-level Student-t model summaries, not participant-level duration effects.

## Factorization and adequacy

The vectorized likelihood represents

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{55}\log t_4(y_j\mid\mu,\sigma).
$$

Concise code does not make passages a probability sample or recover reader-level measurements. Stan can correctly sample the declared posterior even when the declared model is scientifically inadequate. Computation, prior implications, posterior prediction, and the correspondence between rows and modeled units require separate checks.

## Check your understanding

1. Which objects belong in the data block?
2. How do the positivity constraint and half-normal prior differ?
3. What do tilde statements add to `target`?
4. Why does successful sampling not validate the aggregation scheme?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Observed quantities and fixed constants belong in `data`: here $N$, `y`, the two prior scales, and $\nu$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The lower bound defines the parameter's support and transformation; the zero-centered normal density supplies the half-normal prior shape on that support. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Each tilde statement adds the corresponding log-density or log-mass contribution, up to constants, to `target`. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Stan can sample the declared passage-level posterior correctly even if aggregation discarded readers or the likelihood poorly represents the scientific design. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [trace-plot page](checking-markov-chains.qmd) begins the diagnostic sequence using these production draws.
